newsitem.title: USA: Angelica hurt by textile services weakness.
newsitem.headline: Angelica hurt by textile services weakness.

text.p: Angelica Corp said improved manufacturing and marketing business results and positive effects realized in fiscal 1997 from a restructuring charge adopted near the end of the last fiscal year were insufficient to overcome lower earnings in textile services.

In fiscal 1997, Angelica said, the textile services segment had a 22 percent earnings decline on a 2.5 percent increase in revenues. The biggest contributing factor behind the decline was continued margin erosion from greater than expected pressure on prices and margins by health care customers seeking to reduce costs.
Angelica said a few plants also continue to have operating or cost control problems, which hurt earnings.

The company said its Life Retail Stores posted record fiscal 1997 earnings on an 8.4 percent sales increase. The company said it would take steps to enhance the performance of the Life Retail chain to make it a larger factor in the company's results.
In fiscal 1998, Angelica also said it would act to increase volume, maintain or reduce operating costs and strengthen management in both the textile services and manufacturing and marketing segments.

Earlier Tuesday, Angelica reported a fourth-quarter profit of $0.05 per share compared to a loss of $0.85, which included a restructuring charge of $0.95 per share. For the full fiscal year, it earned $0.88 per share compared to earnings of $0.13 in fiscal 1996.
The company provides textile rental and laundry services to health care institutions and manufactures and markets uniforms.
